proofs: Current code-mode custom-tool program is read from canonical Codex rollout bytes while authenticated MCP admission is paused and the entire Connect Store snapshot is still unchanged. It contains the original request_id, step_id, body and wait_for_reply=true before the nested send can dispatch.

The actual initial request context includes the full Connect skill instruction about durably retaining intent. Code mode discovers one installed Connect send method from ALL_TOOLS and awaits the real nested MCP call; there is no handwritten communication transport.

After real acceptance, the public peer sees one original draft and the public owner sees the task Waiting. Codex is killed before the next scripted response, then actual exec resume reopens the exact saved UUID. The peer produces a replay from the original program in actual resumed input, not a replacement prompt or its initial in-memory argument object. One accepted effect/message remains; the full post-acceptance Store snapshot is unchanged.

An interruption before dispatch kills/reaps the actual child and drains the paused MCP listener with an unchanged Store. A replacement listener on the same endpoint and exact-session resume recover the original on-disk program and create one question/message, without replacing the task or conversation.

Revocation after intent persistence but before dispatch denies the original invocation under current authority with no mutation beyond the explicit revocation. A fresh exact-session attempt fails required MCP startup before another scripted request; the authoritative Store remains unchanged.
Across all final cases, model-request traffic contains neither the protected HostSession bearer nor the backing owner credential. Model accounts and live provider keys are not inherited.
